provenance_summary: V1-B biological expansion wave. Fungal biosorption using living or dead fungal biomass for heavy metal and dye removal. Cell wall components (chitin, glucan, mannoprotein) provide abundant binding sites.

mechanisms.description: Fungal cell wall biosorption: chitin, glucan, and mannoprotein in fungal cell wall provide amino, carboxyl, hydroxyl, and phosphate groups for heavy metal coordination

pollutant_feature.text: Heavy metal ions (Pb²⁺, Cu²⁺, Cd²⁺, Zn²⁺, Cr³⁺)
pollutant_feature.quote: In ion exchange mechanism, metal cations bind to a vacant site,

bio_structure.text: Amino (-NH₂), carboxyl (-COOH), hydroxyl (-OH), phosphate groups on fungal cell wall
bio_structure.quote: these groups are present on bacterial cell wall
bio_structure.scope_match: Keywords: amino, groups, wall, hydroxyl, cell

interaction.text: Coordination and electrostatic interaction with cell wall functional groups
interaction.quote: these groups are present on bacterial cell wall
interaction.scope_match: Keywords: interaction, groups, wall, functional, coordination

why_it_works.text: Biosorption capacity varies by species and metal: typically 10-200 mg/g
why_it_works.quote: Recent research outcomes on bacterial biosorption of heavy metals

causal_chain.transferable_principle: Fungal cell wall chitin/glucan/mannoprotein provides abundant functional groups for metal biosorption

mechanisms.name: 真菌细胞壁几丁质/葡聚糖官能团配位生物吸附

engineering_constraints.description: Fungal biomass can be obtained as waste from fermentation industry (antibiotic, enzyme production)

narrative.text: Fungal biosorption exploits the natural metal-binding capacity of fungal cell walls. Both living and dead biomass can be used, with dead biomass avoiding toxicity limitations. Fungal biomass is abundantly available as waste from biotechnology industries.

design_translation.idea: Use fungal biomass (living or dead) from fermentation industry waste as low-cost biosorbent for heavy metal removal from wastewater
design_translation.design_principle: Fungal cell wall contains chitin, glucan, and mannoprotein with amino, carboxyl, and hydroxyl groups for metal biosorption
design_translation.implementation_example: Aspergillus niger for Pb²⁺ biosorption; Saccharomyces cerevisiae for Cu²⁺ biosorption; Penicillium chrysogenum for dye biosorption
design_translation.constraints: Biosorption capacity varies with fungal species and growth conditions; regeneration may degrade biomass
design_translation.target_interaction: metal biosorption via functional group coordination
